column1: # Vocabularies the perf workflow measures. One line here is one family in the
# report — adding a model must not need a change to the workflow, the Rust
# harness or the Python harness, so all three read this file.
# name      what the report calls it.
# ranks     basename of the `.tiktoken` rank file this vocabulary
#           publishes, or `-`. The rank-file family reads what splintr bundles,
#           so the bytes under every engine are provably the ones it ships.
# json      URL of a HuggingFace `tokenizer.json`, or `-` when the model
#           publishes none (Kimi) or bundles ranks only.
# pattern   splintr's own name for the pre-tokenizer expression the rank file is
#           defined by. Required with `ranks`, meaningless without it — a
#           `tokenizer.json` carries its own. Both harnesses resolve this to
#           splintr's exported constant rather than to a transcription, because
#           a hand-typed pattern benchmarks a different pre-tokenizer for every
#           engine at once and parity cannot catch it: they all agree on the
#           wrong answer.
# giga      gigatoken's own name for the scheme, or `-` to leave it out of the
#           rank-file row. Never inferred from the file name: gigatoken looks
#           the scheme up by name and an unrecognised one mistokenizes rather
#           than failing.
# One row per distinct *vocabulary*, not per model family. Timing is a
# property of the merge ranks and the corpus; a family that states another
# family's ranks re-times the identical work and tells you nothing the row it
# copied did not. That is why Phi-4 and OLMo-2 are absent despite being
# bundled — both read cl100k_base's 100,256 ranks, which `cl100k` already
# times — and it is the first question to ask of any row proposed here.
# gpt-oss went the same way, and it is the case that shows the rule is about
# the vocabulary rather than the file: its `tokenizer.json` states o200k_base's
# 199,998 ranks exactly (same content hash) but carries 446,189 merges to
# Xenova's 199,742, so the two files are not byte-equivalent and the row was
# not literally re-timing `o200k`. What it measured with the surplus was JSON
# and merge-table ingestion, not a second vocabulary — for 27.9 MB, the
# largest download here. Correctness coverage is untouched: `perf_parity.py`
# still checks ids against `openai/gpt-oss-20b`.
# Most `tokenizer.json`s come from `hf-internal-testing/tokenizers-test-data`,
# the same repo the upstream `tokenizers` benchmark reads, so a row here is
# comparable with a row there. The two OpenAI vocabularies are not in it and
# come from Xenova's mirrors, and ModernBERT from Answer.AI's own repository.
# name
